newsitem.title: FRANCE: No French budget or VAT income slippage - Arthuis.
newsitem.headline: No French budget or VAT income slippage - Arthuis.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in an interview published on Thursday that there were no signs of budget slippage and that tax revenue, including value added tax revenue, was not below forecast.
"Nothing points to slippage in the state budget," he said in business daily Les Echos. "Tax revenue, especially VAT, is not below forecasts," he said.
Press speculation in recent weeks has suggested that the 1997 budget is under strain on the revenue side, notably suggesting weak VAT revenues.
"If in any case there were any nasty surprises, we would take sufficient measures to control spending levels," Arthuis said in a reiteration of the government line over the past several weeks.
"We have frozen 10 billion francs (of spending credits). If we had to go further we would do it.
He also said: "I have strong hopes that we will also meet our goals on the social (security) accounts," he said.
